image_description: Two translucent teal plastic disposable lighters standing upright against a white background with faint, blurry text-like artifacts. The lighter on the left shows a side profile with a visible metal guard and spark wheel mechanism. The lighter on the right is angled slightly differently, showing the front/top assembly. Both have clear plastic bodies revealing internal components.

artifact_observations.location: Background, primarily right side and bottom left
artifact_observations.reasoning: Faint, nonsensical letter-like shapes and loops float in the white background. They do not form readable words and appear to be AI-generated hallucinations of text or watermarks.
The internal refraction and molding lines on the plastic look slightly soft and inconsistent with real injection-molded plastic sharpness, though not severely distorted.

artifact_observations.location: Top metal guard of the right lighter
artifact_observations.reasoning: The metal wind guard on the right lighter appears slightly fused with the plastic collar, lacking the distinct separation and sharp edges seen in real manufacturing.

selected_experts.reason: To confirm the specific type of lighter (disposable butane) and rule out misclassification as other handheld tools.
To verify the boundary between the translucent plastic and the white background, checking for edge bleeding or halo effects common in AI generation.
To ensure the internal components (tube, liquid) are correctly positioned within the 3D volume of the plastic casing and not floating incorrectly.
To analyze the gibberish shapes in the background to confirm they are non-text artifacts rather than failed OCR attempts or hidden watermarks.

focus_areas: Integrity of the flint wheel mechanism geometry
Connection points between metal guard and plastic body
custom_prompts_for_reflector: Pay close attention to the 'text_gibberish' artifact severity. While faint, it is a strong indicator of generative origin. Also, verify if the internal tube structure aligns physically with the nozzle exit point using geometric depth analysis.
